# cc-fleet shadow-check allowlist
#
# Exact tuple rule — five TAB-separated fields:
# direction	id-glob	kind-glob	project-glob	reason
#
# direction is legacy-only, go-only, or either. The next three fields use
# path.Match globs. Every active entry MUST identify a reviewed deviation
# narrowly (normally by exact chat ID) and MUST carry a non-empty reason.
#
# Verified semantic rule — three TAB-separated fields:
# class	class-name	reason
#
# THE RULE FOR EVERY CLASS BELOW: it must be structurally unable to absorb a
# regression. Each one names the live fact that admits it (gathered
# independently of the diff, in internal/check/candidates.go and
# cmd/cc-fleet/check_command.go) and the bound that caps how many rows it can
# ever cover. A class with a predicate but no bound is how a duplication
# regression hid here once; a class with a bound but no predicate is a glob
# wearing a name.
#
# ── Codex resume rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# All three share one bound: compose emits exactly ONE row per resume lineage,
# so at most one Go-only row per lineage is absolved and a second is a
# duplication regression that stays visible.
#
# - codex-store-only: NO rollout file exists anywhere in the lineage
#   (CodexRolloutFileIDs walks ~/.codex/sessions). The legacy Codex source is a
#   scan of rollout files, so it cannot reach such a thread by any path; Codex
#   0.146.1 stopped writing one for a paginated thread and the state store is
#   now the only record. Verified from the filesystem, never from the diff.
# - codex-120-bound: the lineage owns rollout files, but its root is outside the
#   newest 120 the legacy scan bounds itself to (CodexCandidateIDs, same mtime
#   ordering as `cc_find_meta … | head -120`).
# - codex-legacy-source: the lineage is inside that bound, but the file's first
#   line lacks the exact thread_source:user marker the legacy classifier
#   requires, so it is filed as a subagent worker. Go takes the state store's
#   classification instead.
#
# ── Codex machine-spawned rows (the mirror-image, legacy-only) ────────────────
# - codex-machine-spawned: the row is LEGACY-only, never Go-only — is_bg keeps
#   a thread out of the DEFAULT listing, never out of --check's own AllView
#   scan, so this class does not exist to cover the ordinary background-thread
#   case (that one already matches on both sides). It exists for a thread the
#   Codex state store excludes from Go's lineage set entirely — its
#   threads.thread_source disagreeing with the rollout file's own meta line,
#   for instance — while the rollout file alone still satisfies the legacy
#   scan. Verified per row against a fresh read-only read of the state store
#   (CodexMachineSpawnedIDs walks threads.source='exec' AND unrenamed,
#   CodexThread.MachineSpawned), never from the diff's own shape: a
#   legacy-only resume-codex row that is NOT machine-spawned stays visible.
#
# ── prompt-count semantics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Bounded by 1:1 pairing — the two rows must agree on id, kind and project and
# differ only in count, so a row missing from one side has no partner and stays
# visible.
#
# - codex-prompt-semantics / claude-prompt-semantics: the legacy count is a grep
#   over token-bearing lines, Go's is parsed complete records; they part company
#   at a partial or injected record.
# - live-prompt-drift: a live chat gained a prompt between the two necessarily
#   sequential snapshots.
# - agent-without-transcript: the whole-row form of the same drift. Go rows a
#   live agent straight from the running process, while the legacy picker names
#   its ⚙ rows out of the transcript STORE — so a subagent spawned while the
#   check runs is on one side until Claude flushes its file. Verified against
#   the store on disk (ClaudeTranscriptIDs walks exactly what `cc_find_meta
#   "$store" -maxdepth 2` walks) and bounded to one row per session id.
#
# ── legacy-side artifacts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# - legacy-cache-empty-cwd: the legacy picker's own name cache holds an EMPTY
#   cwd for this transcript (read read-only from ~/.cc/fleet.db), so it prints
#   the project as "?" while Go re-derives the directory from the file.
#   _cc_metac's incremental branch copies a cached cwd forward untouched, so a
#   chat first seen before it had a parseable user record keeps the blank for
#   life. Bounded by 1:1 pairing on id + kind + prompt count.
# - legacy-socket-squatter: work PARKED on a chat socket — a dev server on the
#   surviving tmux server of a dead chat. Every fleet chat is launched with
#   `new-session -s "$sock"`, so a session under any other name is not a chat;
#   it carries no transcript, which is why it reaches the tuple as a zero-prompt
#   row identified by the socket itself. Bounded by a count taken from the live
#   probe: at most one row per differently named session on that socket, so a
#   real chat's row can never be absorbed.
#
# ── account roster ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# - dormant-account: the Go row lives under an account root the shadow harness
#   never points the reference script at. Verified against the CANONICAL root
#   path, because ~/.cc/2/projects and ~/.cc/3/projects are symlinks back to
#   account 1's store on this fleet — counting those as unreachable would hide a
#   chat the legacy picker does list.
#
# Example (commented; replace with an observed exact ID, never a wildcard):
# go-only	00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000	resume-codex	my-project	legacy 120-rollout candidate bound

class	codex-store-only	the lineage owns no rollout file at all, and the legacy Codex source can only scan rollout files
class	codex-120-bound	legacy examines only its newest 120 rollout files; exactly one Go row is allowed per verified thread lineage
class	codex-legacy-source	legacy requires thread_source:user on the first line while Go takes the state store's classification of the thread
class	codex-machine-spawned	the state store excludes this thread from Go's lineage set while the rollout file alone still satisfies the legacy scan; verified per row against a fresh read of the state store
class	codex-prompt-semantics	legacy grep counts token-bearing rollout lines while Go counts parsed complete user_message records
class	claude-prompt-semantics	legacy byte-tail grep and Go parsed complete-record prompt counts differ at partial or injected records
class	live-prompt-drift	a live chat gained a prompt between the sequential legacy and Go snapshots
class	agent-without-transcript	the agent's process is live but its transcript is not in the store yet, so legacy has nothing to name a row from
class	legacy-cache-empty-cwd	the legacy name cache holds an empty cwd for this transcript, so it prints project "?" while Go reads the directory from the file
class	legacy-socket-squatter	legacy lists every tmux session on a chat socket; a session not named after its socket is parked work, not a chat, and Go does not row it
class	dormant-account	legacy walks only account 1 while Go indexes account roots that canonicalise elsewhere
